request.spec:
Show on each person their score: their settled figures (the due of their SETTLED claims that
count) divided by 100, minus 5 for every overdue claim of theirs that counts, rounded half to even
to a whole number (shown with no decimals, a minus sign when negative).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their score: their settled figures (the due of their SETTLED claims that
count) divided by 100, minus 5 for every overdue claim of theirs that counts, rounded half to even
to a whole number (shown with no decimals, a minus sign when negative).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now shows a **Score** (`person-score`), and all 4 tests in the spec pass under `bin/e2e`. After that run I only reworded one code comment, so I didn't run the tests again.

**The score:** it's settled figures ÷ 100 − 5 × the number of overdue claims that count, rounded half to even and shown as a whole number with a minus sign when negative. For example, Ada with 225.00 settled and nothing overdue scores 2, and Ben with nothing settled and one overdue claim scores −5. It's worked out on screen from figures the person list already has: the settled due total and the overdue claims. So nothing changed in the stored data, the server or the audit file. The code is `scoreOf` in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. The maths uses whole numbers, so exact halves like 2.5 round to the even number.

**A second change you didn't ask for:** scenario 3 failed every time at a step before any score check. A user with the "restricted" role (`wes`) quick-adds a new person, "Dot", and the test expects Dot's row to appear right away. The app already hid people from restricted users unless they share a crew, and `wes` has no person of their own, so the row never appeared. The test also expects Dot to disappear once the sheet is re-loaded. My fix is narrow: anyone a user quick-adds stays on their list until the sheet is next loaded. Nothing else about what restricted users see has changed. This alters existing role behaviour, so check it's what you want.
